comparison: Perfect agreement on purification methodology (C46-C57). Both evaluations recognize this as a major methodological achievement enabling the study. OpenEval emphasizes technical validation details while peer reviewers highlight it as a key contribution to the field.

Strong agreement on ATP-dependent and -independent cleavage activities (C58-C61, C66, C74-C76). Both find the kinetic data convincing with proper controls. OpenEval notes quantified rates and experimental design; peer reviewers praise the rigorous kinetic analysis and substrate preferences.

Both support findings on DRH-1's dominant role in ATP hydrolysis (C6-C7, C48, C78-C79, C169). OpenEval emphasizes the hierarchy established by Walker A mutations; peer reviewers explicitly note 'DRH-1 promotes ATP hydrolysis' as a key finding from detailed kinetic analysis.

Both support RDE-4's essential role (C50, C80, C176-C179). OpenEval focuses on quantified binding affinities and loss of cleavage activity; peer reviewers identify RDE-4 as 'essential to dsRNA processing' and 'critical for cleavage' as major discoveries.

Agreement on autoinhibition model (C8, C140, C147-C149). OpenEval finds deletion analysis and structural data compelling with appropriate RIG-I analogy; peer reviewers explicitly recognize 'discovery of an autoinhibitory role of DRH-1's N-terminal domain' as a strength.

Divergent confidence levels on cryo-EM structure (C9, C102-C109). OpenEval finds 6.1 Å resolution sufficient for domain-level architecture supporting biochemical findings; peer reviewers express concern about 'only medium resolution' and 'limited insight due to limited structural resolution.'

Divergent assessments of high-resolution structure (C116-C125). OpenEval finds 2.9 Å data compelling for detailed helicase motif interactions and translocation model; peer reviewers note it 'only reveals helicase and CTD domains' with 'no information on dsRNA termini recognition' and 'seems detached from general flow.'

Agreement on processivity evidence (C151-C156, C192). OpenEval notes trap experiments show modest but appropriate effect with strong support from internal siRNA analysis; peer reviewers explicitly list trap experiments revealing processive cleavage as a strength.

Agreement on comparative kinetics with dmDcr2 (C165-C168). OpenEval notes striking similarity in rate constants but acknowledges comparison relies on literature values; peer reviewers accept these comparative findings as part of rigorous kinetic analysis without challenge.

Both address integrated mechanistic model (C10, C141, C182-C189). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculation about unobserved intermediates despite well-supported components; peer reviewers SUPPORT the NTD-helicase interaction relieving autoinhibition as a key finding backed by structural and biochemical data.

Agreement on 5'p vs 5'ppp substrate processing (C70-C73). OpenEval finds direct experimental comparison appropriate and important for understanding specificity differences; peer reviewers accept this as part of thorough substrate characterization without challenge.

Agreement on gel-shift binding analyses (C81-C94). OpenEval finds systematic approach with quantified affinities and ATP effects well-supported; peer reviewers accept these as part of 'detailed kinetic analysis' providing 'insight into contribution of each subunit.'

OpenEval supports 2',3'-cyclic phosphate blocking experiments (C95-C101) as clever design dissecting Platform•PAZ versus helicase contributions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

Both address pre-cleavage structure (C110-C113, C196-C198). OpenEval finds interpretation reasonable based on comparison to human Dicer; peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY due to resolution limitations, with interpretation as 'pre-dicing' being speculative and based on analogy.

Agreement on CTD structural features (C133-C139). OpenEval notes structural conservation with RLRs and integration with prior genetic data; peer reviewers support these observations as contributing to understanding RNA-binding interface.

Both address structural features with functional implications (C124-C130). OpenEval supports observations at 2.9 Å with reasonable speculation about phosphorylation; peer reviewers accept speculation as appropriately framed possibility for future investigation.

Both address ΔNTD DRH-1 terminus preference (C150, C170). OpenEval supports quantified rates showing relief of autoinhibition and terminus-dependent activity; peer reviewers accept biochemical data but note broader mechanistic interpretation about self/non-self discrimination remains speculative.

OpenEval supports comparison to literature with reasonable speculation about missing cofactors (C62-C63). No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressing these comparative claims found.

OpenEval supports mechanistic differences from dmDcr2 (C65-C69, C172-C175) with clear phenotypic distinctions. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressing these comparative mechanistic claims found.
OpenEval supports integration with prior in vivo work (C157) strengthening biological relevance. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressing this citation found.
